## There is no `brms` in Julia

- `brms` exists partly because in R you cannot drop the delay
  machinery into a model you wrote yourself. In Julia you can
- So perhaps most people do not need a formula interface. They write
  the model and the composed distribution goes in
- The people who use the R package do not write Julia, and a formula
  is the interface they have
- A Julia `brms` would very likely be more extensible. The
  metaprogramming would not be fighting a second language with no user
  types

::: {.callout-note}
Where is a formula interface still needed, once the components compose
on their own?
:::
